title: Backup: dataset construction
speaker: Either
notes: AssemblyHands keeps frames with valid root and more than 10 valid joints per hand. Ego-Exo4D uses undistorted frames, standardized joint indices and atomic-action windows from -0.5 to +1.0 seconds. For both datasets, half of original validation episodes become the processed test split. EgoMe-pose uses confidence and episode-validity filtering. No new manual annotation audit is reported.

title: Backup: likely questions
speaker: Either
notes: Q: Is future information leaked? A: Future Exo supplies training targets only; test inference uses past Ego inputs. Q: Why not predict Exo pixels? A: Feature reconstruction transfers context with a smaller target, but can inherit encoder bias. Q: Is language useful? A: The task is conditioned on language, but a dedicated language ablation is missing. Q: Does it solve robotics? A: CALVIN feature distillation shows a modest transfer improvement, not end-to-end dexterous real-world deployment.
